### Automated Revenue Service Annual Operating Cost: $150 million {#sec-automated_revenue_service_annual_opex}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Annual operating cost of the Automated Revenue Service: design transaction volume times the all-in comparator-anchored cost per settlement. Uncertainty propagates from the component distributions via Monte Carlo.

**Inputs**:

- [Automated Revenue Service Annual Transaction Volume](#sec-automated_revenue_service_annual_transaction_volume): 500 billion transactions
- [All-In Cost per Settlement Transaction](#sec-automated_revenue_service_all_in_cost_per_transaction): $0.0003 (95% CI: $0.0001 - $0.001)

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cost_{revenue} \\
= N_{tx} \times Cost_{tx} \\
= 500B \times \$0.0003 \\
= \$150M
\end{gathered}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Current Trajectory Average Income at Year 20: $20,483 {#sec-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Average income (GDP per capita) at year 20 under current trajectory trajectory.

**Inputs**:

- [Current Trajectory GDP at Year 20](#sec-current_trajectory_gdp_year_20) 🔢: $188 trillion
- [Global Population 2045 (Projected)](#sec-global_population_2045_projected) 📊: 9.2 billion of people

$$
\begin{gathered}
\bar{y}_{base,20} \\
= \frac{GDP_{base,20}}{Pop_{2045}} \\
= \frac{\$188T}{9.2B} \\
= \$20.5K
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
GDP_{base,20} \\
= GDP_{global} \times (1 + g_{base})^{20} \\
= \$115T \times (1 + 2.5\%)^{20} \\
= \$188T
\end{gathered}
$$
#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*✓ High confidence*

#### Monte Carlo Distribution

{{< include ../figures/mc-distribution-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20.qmd >}}

#### Exceedance Probability

{{< include ../figures/exceedance-current_trajectory_avg_income_year_20.qmd >}}

:::

= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\

### Total DALYs Lost from Disease Eradication Delay: 8.77 billion DALYs {#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_dalys}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total Disability-Adjusted Life Years lost from disease eradication delay (PRIMARY estimate)

**Inputs**:

- [Years of Life Lost from Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yll) 🔢: 7.9 billion years
- [Years Lived with Disability During Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yld) 🔢: 873 million years

$$
DALYs_{lag} = YLL_{lag} + YLD_{lag} = 7.9B + 873M = 8.77B
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
YLL_{lag} \\
= \text{DEATHS\_TOTAL} \times (REMAINING_LIFE_EXPECTANCY_AT_60 - (\text{MEAN\_AGE\_OF\_DEATH} - 60))
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{lag} \\
= T_{lag} \times Deaths_{disease,daily} \times 338 \\
= 8.2 \times 150{,}000 \times 338 \\
= 416M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
YLD_{lag} \\
= Deaths_{lag} \times T_{suffering} \times DW_{chronic} \\
= 416M \times 6 \times 0.35 \\
= 873M
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Years of Life Lost from Disease Eradication Delay: 7.9 billion years {#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yll}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Years of Life Lost from disease eradication delay deaths (PRIMARY estimate). Years lost per death = WHO conditional remaining life expectancy at 60, adjusted down to the mean lag-death age of 62 (~19 years/death). Replaces life-expectancy-at-birth minus age, which mixed an at-birth measure (carrying child mortality the deceased already survived) with a conditional question and understated the loss by ~40%. The linear age adjustment slightly understates remaining years (conditional life expectancy falls by less than one year per year of age).

**Inputs**:

- [Total Deaths from Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_deaths_averted) 🔢: 416 million deaths
- [Remaining Life Expectancy at Age 60 (Global)](#sec-global_life_expectancy_remaining_at_age_60) 📊: 21 years (95% CI: 19.6 years - 22 years)
- [Mean Age of Preventable Death from Post-Safety Efficacy Delay](#sec-regulatory_delay_mean_age_of_death) 📊: 62 years (SE: ±3 years)

$$
\begin{gathered}
YLL_{lag} \\
= \text{DEATHS\_TOTAL} \times (REMAINING_LIFE_EXPECTANCY_AT_60 - (\text{MEAN\_AGE\_OF\_DEATH} - 60))
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{lag} \\
= T_{lag} \times Deaths_{disease,daily} \times 338 \\
= 8.2 \times 150{,}000 \times 338 \\
= 416M
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/tornado-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yll.qmd >}}

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yll.qmd >}}

#### Monte Carlo Distribution

{{< include ../figures/mc-distribution-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_yll.qmd >}}

### Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit): 566x {#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Physical upper bound on trial-capacity multiplier from participant availability. Even with unlimited funding, annual trial enrollment cannot exceed willing participant pool.

**Inputs**:

- [Global Patients Willing to Participate in Clinical Trials](#sec-willing_trial_participants_global) 🔢: 1.08 billion people
- [Annual Global Clinical Trial Participants](#sec-current_trial_slots_available) 📊: 1.9 million patients/year (95% CI: 1.5 million patients/year - 2.3 million patients/year)

$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

{{< include ../figures/tornado-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

{{< include ../figures/sensitivity-table-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical.qmd >}}

### Patients Fundable Annually at Reference Funding: 23.4 million patients/year {#sec-dfda_patients_fundable_annually}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of patients fundable annually at the reference pragmatic trial funding level and empirical pragmatic trial cost. Source-agnostic counterpart of DIH_PATIENTS_FUNDABLE_ANNUALLY.

**Inputs**:

- [Reference Annual Trial Subsidies](#sec-dfda_trial_subsidies_annual) 🔢: $21.8 billion
- [Pragmatic Trial Cost per Patient](#sec-dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient) 📊: $929 (95% CI: $97 - $3,000)

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,ref} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{trial,ref}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{trial,ref} \\
= Funding_{trial,ref} - OPEX_{trial} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{trial} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

#### Sensitivity Analysis

### Diseases Without Effective Treatment: 6,650 diseases {#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Number of diseases without effective treatment. 95% of 7,000 rare diseases lack FDA-approved treatment (per Orphanet 2024). This represents the therapeutic search space that remains unexplored.

$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650

### Cumulative Efficacy Testing Cost (1962-2024): $4.84 trillion {#sec-efficacy_lag_cumulative_excess_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Cumulative Phase 2/3 efficacy testing cost since 1962. Uses direct Phase 2/3 cost per drug - this is a LOWER BOUND because it excludes opportunity cost of delays, compounds abandoned due to cost barrier, and regulatory overhead.

**Inputs**:

- [Pharma Phase 2/3 Cost Barrier Per Drug](#sec-pharma_phase_2_3_cost_barrier): $1.56 billion (SE: ±$200 million)
- [Total Drugs Approved Since 1962](#sec-drugs_approved_since_1962) 🔢: 3,100 drugs

$$
\begin{gathered}
Cost_{eff,cumul} \\
= Cost_{P2+P3} \times N_{drugs,62} \\
= \$1.56B \times 3{,}100 \\
= \$4.84T
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{drugs,62} \\
= Drugs_{ann,curr} \times 62 \\
= 50 \times 62 \\
= 3{,}100
\end{gathered}
$$

### Total Deaths from Historical Progress Delays: 102 million deaths {#sec-existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_deaths_total}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total deaths from delaying existing drugs over 8.2-year efficacy lag. One-time impact of eliminating Phase 2-4 testing delay for drugs already approved 1962-2024. Based on Lichtenberg (2019) estimate of 12M lives saved annually × 8.2 years efficacy lag. Excludes innovation acceleration effects.

**Inputs**:

- [Annual Lives Saved by Pharmaceuticals](#sec-pharma_lives_saved_annual) 🔢: 12.4 million deaths
- [Regulatory Delay for Efficacy Testing Post-Safety Verification](#sec-efficacy_lag_years) 📊: 8.2 years (SE: ±2 years)

$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{lag,total} \\
= Lives_{saved,annual} \times T_{lag} \\
= 12.4M \times 8.2 \\
= 102M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Lives_{saved,annual} \\
= \frac{LY_{saved,annual}}{T_{ext}} \\
= \frac{149M}{12} \\
= 12.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

### Total Economic Loss from Historical Progress Delays: $290 trillion {#sec-existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_economic_loss}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Total economic loss from delaying existing drugs over 8.2-year efficacy lag. One-time benefit of eliminating Phase 2-4 delay. Excludes innovation acceleration effects. Years lost per death uses WHO conditional remaining life expectancy at 60 adjusted to the mean lag-death age (~19 years/death), not life-expectancy-at-birth minus age, which understated remaining years by ~40%.

**Inputs**:

- [Remaining Life Expectancy at Age 60 (Global)](#sec-global_life_expectancy_remaining_at_age_60) 📊: 21 years (95% CI: 19.6 years - 22 years)
- [Total Deaths from Historical Progress Delays](#sec-existing_drugs_efficacy_lag_deaths_total) 🔢: 102 million deaths
- [Mean Age of Preventable Death from Post-Safety Efficacy Delay](#sec-regulatory_delay_mean_age_of_death) 📊: 62 years (SE: ±3 years)
- [Standard Economic Value per QALY](#sec-standard_economic_qaly_value_usd) 📊: $150,000 (SE: ±$30,000)

$$
\begin{gathered}
Loss_{lag} \\
= \text{DEATHS\_TOTAL} \times (REMAINING_LIFE_EXPECTANCY_AT_60 - (\text{MEAN\_AGE\_OF\_DEATH} - 60)) \times \text{VSLY}
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{lag,total} \\
= Lives_{saved,annual} \times T_{lag} \\
= 12.4M \times 8.2 \\
= 102M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Lives_{saved,annual} \\
= \frac{LY_{saved,annual}}{T_{ext}} \\
= \frac{149M}{12} \\
= 12.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
*~ Medium confidence*

### Ratio of Type II Error Cost to Type I Error Benefit: 3,389:1 {#sec-type_ii_error_cost_ratio}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Ratio of Type II error cost to Type I error benefit (harm from delay vs. harm prevented)

**Inputs**:

- [Total DALYs Lost from Disease Eradication Delay](#sec-dfda_efficacy_lag_elimination_dalys) 🔢: 8.77 billion DALYs
- [Maximum DALYs Saved by FDA Preventing Unsafe Drugs (1962-2024)](#sec-type_i_error_benefit_dalys) 🔢: 2.59 million DALYs

$$
\begin{gathered}
Ratio_{TypeII} \\
= \frac{DALYs_{lag}}{DALY_{TypeI}} \\
= \frac{8.77B}{2.59M} \\
= 3{,}390
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
DALYs_{lag} = YLL_{lag} + YLD_{lag} = 7.9B + 873M = 8.77B
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
YLL_{lag} \\
= \text{DEATHS\_TOTAL} \times (REMAINING_LIFE_EXPECTANCY_AT_60 - (\text{MEAN\_AGE\_OF\_DEATH} - 60))
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{lag} \\
= T_{lag} \times Deaths_{disease,daily} \times 338 \\
= 8.2 \times 150{,}000 \times 338 \\
= 416M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
YLD_{lag} \\
= Deaths_{lag} \times T_{suffering} \times DW_{chronic} \\
= 416M \times 6 \times 0.35 \\
= 873M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
DALY_{TypeI} \\
= DALY_{thal} \times 62 \\
= 41{,}800 \times 62 \\
= 2.59M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
DALY_{thal} \\
= YLD_{thal} + YLL_{thal} \\
= 13{,}000 + 28{,}800 \\
= 41{,}800
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
YLD_{thal} \\
= DW_{thal} \times N_{thal,survive} \times LE_{thal} \\
= 0.4 \times 540 \times 60 \\
= 13{,}000
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{thal,survive} \\
= N_{thal,US,prevent} \times (1 - Rate_{thal,mort}) \\
= 900 \times (1 - 40\%) \\

$$

= Deaths_{thal} \times 80 \\

= 28{,}800
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Deaths_{thal} \\
= Rate_{thal,mort} \times N_{thal,US,prevent} \\
= 40\% \times 900 \\
= 360
\end{gathered}

### First-Principles Optimal US Defense Budget: $184 billion {#sec-us_defense_first_principles_optimal}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

First-principles optimal US homeland-defense budget: the bottom-up sum of what defending the United States actually requires at efficient prices. Nuclear second strike $30B + homeland air/missile defense $35B + Coast Guard $14B + National Guard $30B + cyber defense $15B + mobilization hedge $60B = ~$184B. Honest range ~$130-260B. Compare: current ~$886B. Restraint-school proposals (Posen, Cato) and peer benchmarks land higher (~$450-675B) because they cost reduced hegemony and allied/peer deterrence, not homeland defense.

**Inputs**:

- [First-Principles Defense: Nuclear Second Strike](#sec-us_defense_fp_nuclear_deterrent): $30 billion (95% CI: $20 billion - $50 billion)
- [First-Principles Defense: Homeland Air & Missile Defense](#sec-us_defense_fp_homeland_air_missile): $35 billion (95% CI: $25 billion - $50 billion)
- [First-Principles Defense: Coast Guard](#sec-us_defense_fp_coast_guard): $14 billion (95% CI: $12 billion - $16 billion)
- [First-Principles Defense: National Guard](#sec-us_defense_fp_national_guard): $30 billion (95% CI: $24 billion - $40 billion)
- [First-Principles Defense: Cyber Defense](#sec-us_defense_fp_cyber): $15 billion (95% CI: $10 billion - $25 billion)
- [First-Principles Defense: Mobilization Hedge](#sec-us_defense_fp_mobilization_hedge): $60 billion (95% CI: $40 billion - $100 billion)

$$
\begin{gathered}
D_{optimal} \\
= D_{nuclear} + D_{air} + D_{cg} + D_{guard} + D_{cyber} \\
+ D_{hedge} \\
= \$30B + \$35B + \$14B + \$30B + \$15B + \$60B \\
= \$184B
\end{gathered}
$$

*~ Medium confidence*

### Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation): 100% {#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Wishonia disease-cure fraction over 20 years under full implementation. Uses full trial-capacity scaling and applies an upper bound of 100% of untreated disease classes.

**Inputs**:

- [Diseases Getting First Treatment Per Year](#sec-new_disease_first_treatments_per_year) 📊: 15 diseases/year (95% CI: 8 diseases/year - 30 diseases/year)
- [Pragmatic Trial Capacity Multiplier at Treaty-Scale Funding](#sec-dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier) 🔢: 12.3x
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [Maximum Trial Capacity Multiplier (Physical Limit)](#sec-dfda_max_trial_capacity_multiplier_physical) 🔢: 566x
- [Diseases Without Effective Treatment](#sec-diseases_without_effective_treatment) 🔢: 6,650 diseases
- [1% Reduction in Military Spending/War Costs from Treaty](#sec-treaty_reduction_pct): 1%

$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1, \frac{Treatments_{new,ann} \times \min\left(\frac{k_{capacity} \times s_{mil,max}}{Reduce_{treaty}}, k_{capacity,max}\right) \times 20}{N_{untreated}}\right) \\
= \min\left(1, \frac{15 \times \min\left(\frac{12.3 \times 87.6\%}{1\%}, 566\right) \times 20}{6{,}650}\right) \\
= 100\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity} \\
= \frac{N_{fundable,ref}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{23.4M}{1.9M} \\
= 12.3
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,ref} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{trial,ref}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{trial,ref} \\
= Funding_{trial,ref} - OPEX_{trial} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{trial} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
s_{mil,max} = Cut_{WW2} = 87.6\% = 87.6\%
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$
#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*✓ High confidence*

#### Monte Carlo Distribution

\begin{gathered}
Cut_{WW2} \\
= 1 - \frac{Spending_{US,1947}}{Spending_{US,1945}} \\
= 1 - \frac{\$176B}{\$1.42T} \\
= 87.6\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
f_{cure,20,wish} \\
= \min\left(1, \frac{Treatments_{new,ann} \times \min\left(\frac{k_{capacity} \times s_{mil,max}}{Reduce_{treaty}}, k_{capacity,max}\right) \times 20}{N_{untreated}}\right) \\
= \min\left(1, \frac{15 \times \min\left(\frac{12.3 \times 87.6\%}{1\%}, 566\right) \times 20}{6{,}650}\right) \\
= 100\%
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity} \\
= \frac{N_{fundable,ref}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{23.4M}{1.9M} \\
= 12.3
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{fundable,ref} \\
= \frac{Subsidies_{trial,ref}}{Cost_{pragmatic,pt}} \\
= \frac{\$21.8B}{\$929} \\
= 23.4M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
Subsidies_{trial,ref} \\
= Funding_{trial,ref} - OPEX_{trial} \\
= \$21.8B - \$40M \\
= \$21.8B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
OPEX_{trial} \\
= Cost_{platform} + Cost_{staff} + Cost_{infra} \\
+ Cost_{regulatory} + Cost_{community} \\
= \$15M + \$10M + \$8M + \$5M + \$2M \\
= \$40M
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
k_{capacity,max} \\
= \frac{N_{willing}}{Slots_{curr}} \\
= \frac{1.08B}{1.9M} \\
= 566
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{willing} \\
= N_{patients} \times Pct_{willing} \\
= 2.4B \times 44.8\% \\
= 1.08B
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
N_{untreated} \\
= N_{rare} \times 0.95 \\
= 7{,}000 \times 0.95 \\
= 6{,}650
\end{gathered}
$$
where:
$$
\begin{gathered}
GDP_{base,20} \\
= GDP_{global} \times (1 + g_{base})^{20} \\
= \$115T \times (1 + 2.5\%)^{20} \\
= \$188T
\end{gathered}
$$
*✓ High confidence*

### Wishonia Trajectory GDP at Year 20: $10.7 quadrillion {#sec-wishonia_trajectory_gdp_year_20}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Projected global GDP at year 20 under the Wishonia Trajectory. Model applies all Wishonia policy channels and redirects the full Political Dysfunction Tax non-health opportunity pool to highest-marginal-value uses. Health recovery is modeled separately through disease burden removal to avoid overlap. Military and non-health reallocation effects are ramped at 50% intensity for the first 3 years, then 100% for years 4-20, reflecting implementation lag. Military reallocation uses a physically demonstrated upper bound (post-WW2 demobilization) rather than an arbitrary policy cap.

**Inputs**:

- [Global GDP (2025)](#sec-global_gdp_2025) 📊: $115 trillion
- [Baseline Global GDP Growth Rate](#sec-gdp_baseline_growth_rate): 2.5%
- [Wishonia Military Reallocation Physical Max Share](#sec-wishonia_military_reallocation_physical_max_share) 🔢: 87.6%
- [GDP Growth Boost at 30% Military Reallocation](#sec-military_redirect_gdp_boost_at_30pct): 5.5% (95% CI: 3.5% - 7.5%)
- [R&D Spillover Multiplier](#sec-rd_spillover_multiplier): 2x (95% CI: 1.5x - 2.5x)
- [Wishonia Disease Cure Fraction (20yr, Full Implementation)](#sec-wishonia_disease_cure_fraction_20yr_full) 🔢: 100%
- [Disease Burden as % of GDP](#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct) 📊: 13%
- [Global R&D Misallocation Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_science_opportunity_cost) 📊: $4 trillion (95% CI: $2 trillion - $10 trillion)
- [Global Lead Poisoning Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_lead_opportunity_cost) 📊: $6 trillion (95% CI: $4 trillion - $8 trillion)
- [Global Migration Opportunity Cost](#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost) 📊: $57 trillion (95% CI: $5 trillion - $170 trillion)
- [Economic Multiplier for Healthcare Investment](#sec-economic_multiplier_healthcare_investment) 📊: 4.3x (95% CI: 3x - 6x)
- [Economic Multiplier for Military Spending](#sec-economic_multiplier_military_spending) 📊: 0.6x (95% CI: 0.4x - 0.9x)

$$
GDP_{wish,20}=GDP_0(1+g_{ramp})^{3}(1+g_{full})^{17}
$$

*✓ High confidence*

### Disease Burden as % of GDP: 13% {#sec-disease_burden_gdp_drag_pct}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Fraction of GDP currently lost to disease (productivity losses + medical costs diverted from productive use). $5T productivity loss + $9.9T direct medical costs = $14.9T on $115T GDP = ~13%. As diseases are progressively cured, this drag is recovered as GDP growth. This is the missing factor that makes the treaty trajectory look like a singularity rather than a modest improvement.

**Source**: [@disease-economic-burden-109t]

#### Uncertainty Range

**Technical**: Distribution: Fixed

*✓ High confidence*

### Remaining Life Expectancy at Age 60 (Global): 21 years {#sec-global_life_expectancy_remaining_at_age_60}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Additional years a person alive at age 60 can expect to live, global both-sexes (WHO life tables: 21.0 years in 2019; 19.6 in COVID-depressed 2021). This is CONDITIONAL remaining life expectancy, not life-expectancy-at-birth minus age: at-birth figures carry child mortality that someone who reached 60 already survived, so subtracting an age from them understates remaining years by roughly 40% at this age. Used for years-of-life-lost per efficacy-lag death. The GBD reference life table would give more (~23 years at 60); WHO period tables are the lower of the two standard choices.

**Source**: [@who-gho-life-expectancy-age-60-2021]

#### Uncertainty Range

### Global Migration Opportunity Cost: $57 trillion {#sec-political_dysfunction_global_migration_opportunity_cost}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Unrealized output from migration restrictions. Clemens (2011) estimated eliminating labor mobility barriers could increase global GDP by 50-150%. At $115T global GDP, Clemens lower bound = $57T; upper bound = $170T. The estimate is controversial: critics argue it assumes full global labor mobility and ignores fiscal and social adjustment costs. Skeptical lower bound: ~$5T (partial reforms only). Even 5% workforce mobility would generate trillions, exceeding all foreign aid ever given. This is the largest and most uncertain single component of the dysfunction tax.

**Source**: [@political-dysfunction-tax-paper-2025]

### First-Principles Defense: Mobilization Hedge: $60 billion {#sec-us_defense_fp_mobilization_hedge}

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="📊 Details"}

Mobilization hedge: defense R&D, a maintained industrial base, and a professional cadre force. The WWII lesson is to maintain the capacity to scale, not a standing empire: a peer buildup gives years of warning, and the US went from the 17th-ranked army in 1939 to victory in four years.
